label: early original-phase token (z/b/f/n/3/r/w) right after the bigram "l 1"
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.008% of steps) that fires almost only in the original phase at t=2..5, mostly t=3. The core context is the input bigram "l 1" (prev2=l: 27x lift, prev=1: 24x lift) followed by one of z/b/f/n/3/r/w. The strongest activations are on sequences that start "w l 1 X", "l l 1 X", "g l 1 X" or "z l 1 X", so the first token also matters: precision goes up to 0.77 when first_tok is in {w,l,g,z}, but recall drops. About half the activation mass falls on looser variants of the same context, like "l l l f", "g l 3 n", "w l z 1 3" and "l 1 l z", which are weaker (about 0.6 of max). These are an early l plus a 1, 3 or repeated l, with no single clean rule. It does not fire at t=0..1, at the delimiter, or later in sequences; it fires in the copy phase only in a few rare cases. After "l 1", tokens such as e/p/j/0/2/s/h/m mostly do not fire it.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=w (+4.71), prev2_tok=l (+3.51), prev_tok=1 (+3.40), orig0=g (+3.02), phase=0 & in_tok=n (+2.79), in_tok=w (+2.74). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.59), prev2_tok=w (-2.04), orig_idx=-1 (-1.33), in_first=0 (-0.68).
